title: Hamlet — "To be, or not to be" Soliloquy
author: William Shakespeare
source: The Tragedy of Hamlet, Prince of Denmark. The Folger Shakespeare Library Edition, based on the First Folio (1623) and Second Quarto (1604–1605)
selection_notes: Act 3, Scene 1, lines 64–98. The complete "To be, or not to be" soliloquy. This is the most famous passage in English literature and presents a self-contained philosophical meditation on existence, suffering, and the fear of death. The extract provides rich semantic structure: existential dilemma, enumeration of life's hardships, and the psychological mechanism of conscience inhibiting action. Line breaks follow standard modern editorial practice.
normalization_notes: Spelling modernized per standard editorial practice (e.g., 'pourne' → 'bourne', 'pith' → 'pitch', 'dispriz'd' → 'despised'). Contractions preserved ('tis, th'oppressor's, th'unworthy). The text follows the widely accepted conflated text that combines Folio and Quarto readings. No silent emendations beyond standard editorial modernization.
